name: Schwendt
kurzbeschreibung: A charming village surrounded by untouched nature and the famous Schwendter Seen – a hidden gem in the Kaiserwinkel.
beschreibung:
Overview

Schwendt is situated at an elevation of 702 meters in the Kaiserwinkl holiday region in the Kitzbühel district of northeastern Tyrol. Snuggled at the foot of Mount Unterberghorn (1,773 m) and Mount Feldberg (1,813 m), the village lies beneath the northern limestone crags of the Zahmer Kaiser range. Home to approximately 915 residents, Schwendt is the most peaceful and pristine of the Kaiserwinkl villages, nestled in the scenic Kohlental valley along the Kohlenbach stream. Unlike more bustling alpine resorts, Schwendt preserves an authentic rural heritage with historic farmsteads, traditional community life, and supreme tranquility. Its gentle Alpine terrain makes it an insider tip for hikers, nature lovers, and cross-country skiing enthusiasts.

History

The name Schwendt stems from the Middle High German word schwenden, referring to the clearing of woodland through slash-and-burn practices. Archaeological discoveries, including a Bronze Age flanged axe, confirm ancient routes through the valley. The settlement was first documented between 1180 and 1190 as Oberswente in records of Fischbachau Abbey. The Kohlental valley owes its name to centuries of charcoal burning and historical lead and iron mining that continued until the late 19th century. The late Gothic parish church dedicated to Saint Giles was consecrated in 1506 over 13th-century Romanesque foundations. It boasts a monumental Saint Christopher fresco from around 1510 on the northern exterior wall, an elaborate Baroque high altar from 1700, and a delicate Rococo pulpit.

Getting there

Schwendt is easily reachable by road, often toll-free from southern Germany. Drivers arriving from Munich can exit the A93 motorway at Oberaudorf/Niederndorf, taking state road B172 via Walchsee to Kössen, before continuing along the B176 directly into Schwendt. From Innsbruck or Salzburg, take the A12 to Kufstein Süd, following the B173, B178, and B176 through St. Johann in Tirol. Train travelers arrive at international rail hubs in Kufstein or St. Johann in Tirol. VVT bus line 800 operates regularly between St. Johann and Schwendt. Visitors holding the Kaiserwinkl Card enjoy complimentary regional bus travel.

Tips

In winter, glide along the scenic Kohlental cross-country ski trail, connected to the wider 120-kilometer Kaiserwinkl Nordic skiing network. During the summer months, embark on a summit hike up Mount Feldberg (1,813 m) via the Scheibenbichlalm pasture for panoramic views of the Kaisergebirge rocky precipices. Admire the outdoor frescoes of Saint Giles parish church and explore the riverside Kohlental path. A short trip brings you to the Schwemm nature reserve, North Tyrol’s largest peat bog, featuring an observation tower and educational boardwalks. Conclude your day with traditional Tyrolean dumplings at the historic Schwendterwirt inn.
